_doc: Single source for SD-97's technology choices (compact cut). Read by video/src/stack.py for the 5.1 technology slides, the stack table, the fix-slide 'Rejected' lines and the C4 technology labels, and by `stack.py sync` for the booklet and OUTLINE.md regions.

stack.heading: Telemetry log: Kafka, keyed by vehicle ID
stack.title: Kafka keyed by vehicle: even load and per-vehicle order
stack.pick: Kafka, 512 partitions, keyed by vehicle ID
stack.why: Even load, and each vehicle's messages in order on one partition.
stack.how: Topic `positions`, partition = hash(vehicle); a separate `safety` topic. Three days on the brokers.
stack.detail: 300 MB/s at peak, 900 MB/s with replication. Keying by geo cell was rejected: a vehicle crossing a cell boundary would change partitions, losing per-vehicle order, and a stadium's cell would be one hot partition.
rejected: Hot partitions; a moving vehicle loses its order.
An honest equal with ordering keys.
stack.course: building-blocks course, part 10 §10.2 and §10.6 (partitioned logs, ordering)

stack.heading: Live store: the SD-39 index, holding vehicles instead of drivers
stack.title: The latest position per vehicle, in memory, by H3 cell
stack.pick: Go service, in memory, H3 res 9, per city
stack.why: Only the latest matters, and 2 M vehicles fit in 400 MB.
stack.how: vehicle → (cell, position, seq) and cell → vehicles, with per-cell change counters. Older seq is dropped.
stack.detail: The same design as SD-39's location index, at resolution 9 because the map zooms further in. Hot cells (> 300 vehicles) are split further; each cell also keeps a count at resolutions 6 and 7 for zoomed-out maps.
rejected: No per-cell change feed, no expiry per member.
stack.course: building-blocks course, part 6 §6.5 (hot keys) and SD-39 (location index)

stack.heading: Map API: viewports subscribe to cells
stack.title: A viewport is a set of cells; the server pushes what changed
stack.pick: Go, WebSockets, a 1 s push tick
stack.why: Deltas for subscribed cells cost far less than every client polling.
stack.how: A viewport maps to cells at its zoom's resolution; each second the server pushes changes, or counts when zoomed out.
stack.detail: About 5,000 concurrent viewers. At city zoom a viewport is ~100 resolution-7 cells sent as counts; at street zoom ~50 resolution-9 cells sent as vehicles. A viewer pans: subscribe the new cells, send their snapshot, then deltas.
rejected: 5,000 scans of the hottest cells a second.
summary: deltas per cell; counts when zoomed out

stack.heading: History lake: Iceberg, partitioned by day and vehicle bucket
stack.title: History laid out for “one vehicle, one hour”
stack.pick: Iceberg on GCS, Parquet, day × 256 vehicle buckets
stack.why: One vehicle's hour becomes one bucket and a range read.
stack.how: Partitioned by (event day, hash(vehicle) mod 256), sorted by vehicle and seq; late positions go to their event day.
stack.detail: About 52 TB a month at ~50 bytes a position, 1.25 PB for two years. ML training reads whole days in bulk; audits read one bucket and filter. Snapshots pin what a replay read.
rejected: One replay scans everyone; late fixes land in the wrong hour.
Not for 10¹² positions with per-vehicle replay.
summary: one vehicle's hour is a range read
stack.course: building-blocks course, part 7 §7.10 (blob layout) and part 14 §14.9 (columnar storage)

1: Writing every arriving position to the live store
a three-minute-old buffered fix overwrites the position from one second ago.
2: Keying the log by geo cell
a stadium's cell becomes one hot partition and vehicles lose their order as they move.
3: 5,000 viewers scan the hottest cells every second.
4: the map stays three minutes behind for the whole flush, and safety events queue behind history.
5: a vehicle's hour is spread over every file that arrived late, and one replay scans everyone.
6: lag can be zero while a vehicle on the map is 40 seconds stale.
